target_customer: Southeast Asian consumers buying furniture and home renovation online, and the merchants who offered 0 percent installment financing
problem: Consumers wanted to spread larger home purchases over time at no extra cost, and small retailers lacked a way to offer it.
business_model: Buy now pay later: merchant fees on 0 percent interest installment loans, underwritten with AI credit models

founders.name: Ed Chin
founders.background_notes: Traded distressed credit on Wall Street and led AI credit underwriting at OctiFi, per YC page.

founders.name: Amit Kumar
founders.background_notes: Backend engineering plus UI and UX.

competitors.name: Rely
competitors.what: First Singapore buy now pay later service, launched 2016

competitors.name: Hoolah
competitors.what: Singapore BNPL service launched 2017 with three month plans

competitors.name: Grab PayLater
competitors.what: BNPL tied to the Grab app, four month plans, online only

technical_complexity.rationale: Credit underwriting models, loan servicing and merchant integrations for a lending product, standard for fintech but needing credit data and risk skill.

defensibility.rationale: Underwriting data could compound but Rely, Hoolah, Atome and Grab already competed, and licensing and funding costs favored larger players.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Well funded rivals already served Singapore; OctiFi instead sold to Latitude Financial in 2021 and became LatitudePay Singapore.

market_need_then: Singapore BNPL uptake rose with the pandemic shift to online shopping per a 2021 Milieu article, and OctiFi launched its service in July 2020.

branding.domain_note: octifi.com is now parked on a GoDaddy for sale page.

identity.voice_and_tone: Instant 0 percent interest loans for responsible spenders

rebrands.why: Acquired by Latitude Financial and folded into its LatitudePay brand

branding.community_and_virality: Listed in Seedly's Singapore BNPL comparison with Atome, Grab PayLater and Hoolah; no sign of a fan community.

brand_strength.rationale: Appeared in consumer comparison guides but the name is spelled like octopus and OctaFX names, and the brand was retired after the acquisition.

outcome_analysis: OctiFi launched in July 2020, joined YC in winter 2021 and was bought by Latitude Financial, closing in November 2021 and becoming LatitudePay Singapore. Aggregators report a deal value of 18.4 million dollars, unverified. A CB Insights profile says LatitudePay later ceased operations with no date. The cause is not public; the macro downturn tag is a low confidence inference from the 2022 to 2023 BNPL pullback.
notes: No funding round is verified by two outlets. Unverified aggregator figures: YC 125K (Dealroom), a 2M seed and 2.13M total (CB Insights), 18.4M acquisition price closing 2021-11-15 (single snippet), and a 4.5M raise from Antler and Emo Capital not clearly tied to OctiFi. Competitor source is an undated Singsaver guide giving launch years 2016 and 2017, so source_date is null. The ceased operations report has no date and the macro_downturn factor is speculative. octifi.com redirects to a domain for sale page. Update: one seed round recorded (March 2021, amount not given) from Seedtable alone; CB Insights reports a 2M seed and 2.13M total, unreconciled and not recorded as an amount.
